inputs.prompt:
A first-person bicycle camera — handlebar grips and the rider's hands ALWAYS VISIBLE at the bottom of the frame, camera locked at exactly 1.6 meters above the ground, NEVER rising, no aerial view, no drone shot — stands stopped at a stone plaza junction in a Yuanmingyuan-style imperial garden park, exactly as in the first frame: the tree-lined path continues straight ahead, and a narrow stone causeway branches off to the LEFT toward the ornamental lake, seen from rider height.

The bicycle stays parked at the SAME SPOT for the entire clip; the rider only turns the handlebar and the view rotates IN PLACE — it does NOT ride forward.

MANDATORY TIMELINE (total 5.2 seconds):
- 0.0s-0.5s: hold still, handlebar in frame, then begin yawing LEFT at a constant rate.
- 0.5s-4.0s: the view pans smoothly and continuously LEFT around the fixed position; the path ahead sweeps toward the right edge; the causeway and the lake pivot in from the left, all at eye level.
- 4.0s-5.2s: rotation complete — a FULL 90 degrees LEFT. The camera now faces straight along the stone causeway at 1.6 m height; lake water with lotus leaves is visible on BOTH sides of the view; handlebar and hands still in frame. Hold this heading.

The 90-degree in-place rotation is the single most important goal. No forward motion, no cuts, no dissolves, no camera rise. Photorealistic park scenery, summer daylight.
